title: Cell Counting and Viability Assessment of 2D and 3D Cell Cultures
author: Piccinini, Tesei, et al.
materials: detached the cells from the flask by trypsinization;

To assess the TB reliability we prepared 8 25-cm2 flasks (called A
i, i = 1, …, 8) containing A549 cells (cells at the 36th passage) and 5 25-cm2 flasks (called P
k, k = 1, …, 5) containing PANC-1 cells (cells at the 116th passage). A549 and PANC-1 are well known and widely used commercial cancer cell lines (American Type Culture Collection - ATCC, Rockville, MD, USA). A549, a lung adenocarcinoma cell line of regular-shaped cells, was adhesion-cultured in Kaighn’s modification of Ham’s F-12 medium (F12 K, ATCC) and supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS, EuroClone, Milan, Italy), 1% penicillin/streptomycin (GE Healthcare, Milan, Italy) and 2% amphotericin B (Euroclone). PANC-1, an epithelioid cell line derived from a human pancreatic carcinoma of ductal cell origin, was grown in medium composed of DMEM/Ham’s F12 (1:1) (Euroclone) supplemented with 10% fetal calf serum (FCS, Euroclone), 2 mM glutamine (Euroclone) and 10 mg/ml insulin (Sigma-Aldrich, St. Louis, MO, USA). All the cells were maintained in an incubator at 5% CO2 humidified atmosphere at 37 °C and checked periodically for mycoplasma contamination using the MycoAlertTM Mycoplasma Detection Kit (Lonza, Basel, Switzerland). Once detached from the surface of the flask, cells started losing their morphology and gradually became round.

We used a haemocytometer (Kova glasstic slide with grids, Hycor Biomedical Inc., Fig. 1b) and a commercially available TB preparation (TB solution 0.4%, SIGMA-ALDRICH, Buchs, Switzerland) to perform the counts. A detailed description of the protocol adopted with TB is reported in [11, 21] and [45]. In brief, for each Ai we:detached the cells from the flask by trypsinization;centrifuged the cell suspension for 5 min at 1200 rpm;resuspended the pellet in 1 ml of culture media using a pipette to obtain a single-cell suspension;removed an aliquot of 100 μl;added 100 μl of TB solution 0.4% to obtain a final 1:2 dilution;waited for 5 min to allow the TB to stain the dead cells;counted the cells using a haemocytometer and a light microscope;calculated the percentage of viability and number of cells in the culture by considering the final dilution factor.

We used the σ values obtained for A
i and P
k to estimate the intra-rater reliability of cell viability (Tables 2 and 5, respectively). Given that cell viability is computed as a percentage, the standard deviation can be considered a direct estimation of the error that may occur when TB is used to estimate cell viability. All σ values were lower than 15% for both O
1 and O
2. Furthermore, the average σ values were approximately 5% for A
i and 3% for P
k (last row of Table 2 and Table 5, respectively), indicating the high reliability of the TB assay when used for this purpose. With regard to the inter-rater reliability of cell viability we considered the E% values reported in the second column of Tables 4 and Table 7. It is worthy of note that the mean cell viability values estimated by O
1 and O
2 for each A
i/P
k were fairly similar (from left, the second and the forth column of Table 2 and Table 5). Accordingly, E% values reported in Table 4 and Table 7 were very low, i.e. <10%, and their average was <5% (last row, second column of Table 4 and Table 7).

With regard to the analysis of cell population density, both intra- and inter-rater variability were once again exceptionally high. The majority of CVs reported in Table 9 were >20%, O
2 never obtaining a CV 15%, with an average E% of 17.23%. Notably, the CV value obtained by O
2 for SP
2, SP
5, SP
6, SP
7 was triple that obtained by O
1 because the total number of living cells counted by O
2 for these SP
i was much more variable than that of the counts performed by O
1. Specifically, the σ of the counts performed by O
2 was more than twice that of the counts performed by O
1. Furthermore, O
2 counted a lower number of cells than O
1 for all but SP
4, probably because there were more cell clusters in the samples prepared by O
2 that must not be considered when counting with a haemocytometer (here, we remark that each operator prepared her/his own 5 S
k). This resulted in a lower μ of the number of living cells counted by O
2 which negatively contributed to the estimation of the CV values. Although both operators are biologists with more than 10 years’ experience in counting cells, the results are suggestive of a greater ability of O
1 to resuspend the samples generated from 3D spheroids, effectively disgregating the cell clusters. This is indicative of the high subjectivity of the TB assay and of it poor reliability when used to estimate the total number of cells in a culture. However, as happened for the 2D cell cultures, almost all p-values computed for viability and total number of living cells were >0.05, once more proving that the sets of counts obtained by the different operators did not significantly differ from each other.

steps.title: Prepare 2D cell culture flasks
steps.instruction: Seed eight 25‑cm² flasks (A_i, i=1…8) with A549 cells at passage 36 in Kaighn’s F12 K medium supplemented with 10 % FBS, 1 % penicillin/streptomycin, and 2 % amphotericin B; seed five 25‑cm² flasks (P_k, k=1…5) with PANC‑1 cells at passage 116 in DMEM/F12 (1:1) supplemented with 10 % fetal calf serum, 2 mM glutamine, and 10 mg ml⁻¹ insulin; incubate all flasks at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, humidified atmosphere and monitor for mycoplasma contamination with the MycoAlert™ kit.

steps.title: Apply thermal shock to A_i flasks
steps.instruction: After 24 h incubation, subject each A_i flask to a specific thermal treatment: A1 and A2 – move to a sterile laminar flow hood at room temperature; A3 and A4 – perform one freeze‑thaw cycle (37 °C incubator → –80 °C freezer → 37 °C incubator) with 15 min (A3) or 30 min (A4) freezer time; A5 and A6 – repeat the freeze‑thaw cycle twice; A7 and A8 – repeat the freeze‑thaw cycle three times. Carry out all shocks sequentially in the morning and count all samples in the afternoon of the same day.

steps.title: Treat P_k flasks with gemcitabine
steps.instruction: Expose P1 (untreated control) and P2–P5 to gemcitabine at final concentrations of 5 µM (P2), 50 µM (P3), 500 µM (P4), and 1000 µM (P5) for 1 h, then wash out and incubate for 72 h before analysis.

steps.title: Generate 3D spheroids in RCCS bioreactor
steps.instruction: Prepare a single‑cell suspension of A549 cells at ~1 × 10⁶ cells ml⁻¹, load 50 ml of this suspension into each rotating chamber of the RCCS‑8DQ bioreactor placed inside a 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ humidified incubator; start rotation at 12 rpm and increase speed as spheroids grow to prevent sedimentation; change culture medium every 4 days; after 15 days spheroids reach 0.5–1 mm diameter and are transferred (one spheroid per well) to 96‑well low‑attachment plates containing 100 µl fresh medium; allow an additional 1‑week spheroidization, then image bright‑field using an inverted Olympus IX51 microscope (4×/0.13 NA objective, CCD camera) and process images as described.

steps.title: Digest spheroids to single cells
steps.instruction: Recover each compact spheroid (SP_i, i=1…8) and digest it into a single‑cell suspension using Trypsin/EDTA 1× solution (Euroclone, Milan, Italy).

steps.title: Prepare cell suspension for trypan blue counting
steps.instruction: For each sample (A_i, P_k, or SP_i): detach cells by trypsinization, centrifuge the suspension for 5 min at 1200 rpm, resuspend the pellet in 1 ml culture medium (use 200 µl for spheroid‑derived samples), withdraw 100 µl aliquot, add 100 µl of TB solution 0.4 % (Sigma‑Aldrich) to obtain a 1:2 dilution (for P_k use a final 1:6 dilution as described), and incubate 5 min for dead‑cell staining.

steps.title: Disaggregate cell clumps before counting
steps.instruction: Using a 2 ml serological pipet, gently pipette the stained suspension up and down 30 times (~15 s) to break any cell aggregates.

steps.title: Count cells with haemocytometer
steps.instruction: Load a drop of the prepared suspension onto a Kova glasstic haemocytometer (Hycor Biomedical), count viable (unstained) and dead (blue‑stained) cells under bright‑field illumination with a light microscope, and calculate percentage viability and total viable cell number by applying the appropriate dilution factor.
